sentence: This project studies how an oncoprotein shapes luminal cell identity as prostate cancer forms and what weaknesses that identity has.
This project collects and shares biomarker samples and brain imaging to help detect Alzheimer's disease and related dementias early.
This project builds an instrument that records brain chemicals and electrical activity and can stimulate the brain, then tests it in swine.
This project studies how selfish mutations in reproductive cells cause congenital disorders, using a chromosome that zebra finches keep only in germline cells.
This project studies how beige fat cells form, how a gene called NFIL3 controls this, and how it affects energy balance and glucose control.
This project studies T cells that attack tumors in children with brain tumors, using single-cell RNA sequencing and patient-derived xenograft models.
This project builds a pipeline that uses whole genome sequencing of wastewater to find foodborne pathogens circulating in communities.
This project builds technologies that enrich viruses in human tissue samples, keep microbial context, and make viral sequencing more accurate.
This project tries to find out how antibiotic resistant staphylococci and enterococci survive treatment and how molecules could target them.
This project studies how a protein that regulates epigenetic modification shapes microglial function in Alzheimer's disease, using CRISPR models.
This project studies how glioblastoma uses trigeminal sensory neurons to escape the immune system through a neuropeptide.
This project studies how an RNA binding protein promotes collagen production in hepatic stellate cells and causes liver fibrosis.
This project builds explainable AI methods that recognize fetal distress earlier during birth.
This project manages data and builds statistical methods for studies at an Alzheimer's Disease Research Center.
This project studies how mutations in the RNA splicing machinery cause leukemias and tries to develop therapies for them.
This project studies how two cyclin C kinases help cancer grow, act within the host immune system, and whether blocking them treats cancer.
This project builds microfluidic devices that isolate and analyze markers from liquid biopsies to guide treatment.
This project provides tissue and pathology resources for studying kidney cancer.
This project tries to find small molecules that target slow skeletal myosin-binding protein C to treat a congenital muscle disorder, testing them in mouse models.
This project tests whether transcranial direct current stimulation paired with reappraisal training helps people with Cannabis Use Disorder reduce craving and cannabis use.
